doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Riverside and the New York scene
title: Lee Morgan's first date for Blue Note with Alfred Lion
summary: Philly Joe brings Ware to the Blue Note date with Lee Morgan and Horace Silver; Alfred Lion starts calling him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And I was ... like I say, I was kind of established now, recording with everybody during this period, and one day Philly Joe Billy Joe grabbed me one day and said, "Man, come over here to the Blue Note, and make this date with Lee Morlin and Horace Silver and Billy and myself -- it was Lee's first date day, I believe, doin' it, and we did -- called Lee Morlin, and I was fearful because I'm thinking of all this music that Lee got -- and he said, "Man, there ain't nothing to that," and I said, "Yeah, man, come on," and he showed me the parts, passages, and I went in to it, and what not, because I didn't read the notations and such; I could read the chord changes, though.

But they were teaching me like I never studied. But we got through that beautifully, and Alfred Lyon was very enthused -- he started calling me on quite a few record dates, and I got some calls from Herbie Irving Mann and a whole lot of people, different ones, but they had to get permission from in order to use me, and they signed me up with some options. Oh, but that was part of that New York scene.
